name: tree
purpose: A hierarchical list of nodes, each row a name with an optional glyph and one line of detail, where a parent row folds its children open and closed under a chevron. It renders a nested `items` data structure on its own (recursively, through one internal row template) and follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, so it fits file and object browsers: the objects of a bucket, the source files of a deployment, the routes of an application. Unlike `menu` it navigates data, not the app, and unlike `accordion` its nodes are rows of the same kind at any depth, not panels of free content.
useWhen: Browsing a hierarchy whose depth is not fixed: bucket objects under folders, the source tree of a deployment, functions grouped by application.
Picking one node out of a hierarchy (`selectable`) to show its detail beside the tree.
A hierarchy the user expands piece by piece, where showing every level at once would bury the node they are after.
avoidWhen: Navigation between views of the app → use `menu` inside `sidebar`.
Flat records with several attributes each → use `table`.
A few sections of free content that open and close → use `accordion`.
A two- or three-level directory of destinations on a marketing page → use `column-navigation`.
related: table` — the flat, multi-column view of the same records; switch to it when columns matter more than nesting.
menu` — the hierarchical list for app navigation, with routes and active state instead of selection.
accordion` — disclosure of free content panels rather than rows of one kind.
empty-state` — what the tree renders when `items` is empty.
skeleton` — the rows the tree renders while `loading`.
bestPractices: Give every node an `id` that is unique across the whole tree, not only among its siblings; `v-model:expanded`, `v-model:selected` and focus are keyed by it.
Seed `v-model:expanded` with the path to the node the user is most likely after (the open folder, the selected file), not with every parent.
Keep labels short and put secondary detail (size, count, modified date) in `description` so rows scan as names first.
Use `selectable` only when the selection drives something on the screen (a detail pane, a preview); for a tree whose rows only lead somewhere, listen to `item-click` instead.
Put per-row controls in the `actions` slot (an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`), never inside the `item` slot, so they do not take over the row's activation.

props.name: items
props.doc: Nodes to render; each is `{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; children?: TreeItem[] }`. A node with a non-empty `children` array is a parent.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: Enables single selection: activating a node writes its id to `v-model:selected` and marks it `aria-selected`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders Skeleton rows in place of the tree and sets `aria-busy`.

props.name: emptyTitle
props.doc: Title of the default empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No items`).

props.name: emptyDescription
props.doc: Supporting line under the empty title.

events.name: item-click
events.notes: A node activated: click on its row, or Enter / Space on the focused node. `item` is the consumer's own node object. Fires after `update:selected` when `selectable`. Not fired for a `disabled` node, nor for a click on the chevron or inside the `actions` region.

slots.name: item
slots.scope: { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean }
slots.notes: Replaces the label region of every row (glyph + label + description). The fallback inside the slot renders `item.icon`, `item.label` and `item.description`. `level` is 1 for top-level nodes; `expanded` is false for leaves. The chevron, indentation, row states and the `actions` region stay owned by the tree.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Trailing per-row controls, end-aligned in the row (e.g. an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`). Clicks and keys inside it do not activate the row nor move tree focus. No fallback; when unused, the region is not rendered.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Replaces the default empty state. The fallback inside the slot is `EmptyState` titled by `emptyTitle` with `emptyDescription`.
